_doc: Delhi OSM layers for scripts/fetch-osm-layers.ts. Water bodies, drainage and localities use the NCT bbox (src/cities/delhi/config.ts); rivers are Yamuna-basin scoped, Hathnikund to the Okhla exit.

water-bodies._note: The 3,700 km engineered drain network is tagged water=drain or wastewater; it belongs to the drainage layer.

rivers._note: Delhi's tributaries are engineered: the WYC/Munak carrier and the Najafgarh, Shahdara and Barapullah drains switch between canal and drain tags, hence per-channel waterways. Rivers are checked in order because the canal names contain 'yamuna'; the Eastern Yamuna Canal (also mapped as 'Poorvi Yamuna Nahar') is a UP diversion outside Delhi's supply and would draw a phantom second Yamuna. The box reaches south and west for the Sahibi only; every other channel keeps the earlier box through the layer clip.

OSM's 'Najafgarh Nallah' (way 164095236) runs from Haryana past the jheel; its last reach to the Yamuna is a way OSM names 'Sahibi River' with alt_name 'Najafgarh Nallah', drawn here with the drain. Checked before the Sahibi, so that name lands here.
The reach OSM names 'Sahibi', in Rajasthan and Haryana (about 27.79-28.00 N), hence the box's south and west reach. Its lower engineered course is the Najafgarh drain, drawn under that id.

drainage._note: No official drain GIS is public, so OSM waterway=drain is the network geometry, labelled as a floor. Ditches are roadside noise at city scale; canals are in the rivers layer.

metadata.note: Best available Delhi drain-network geometry: no official drain GIS is public (the IFC 2018 Drainage Master Plan's 3,737 km across 11 agencies exists only as PDF maps). OSM coverage is partial and skews toward large open channels - lengths here are a floor, not the network total.

localities._note: Urban villages (Lal Dora) are still tagged place=village. NDMC and Cantonment localities fall outside the MCD wards by design.
